Comparative Politics.Political Institutions and Governance: Empirical studies of government structures, electoral systems, legislative behavior, and bureaucratic organization using field data, surveys, and experimental interventions.
Comparative Politics.Political Economy: Experimental and observational research on the interaction of politics and economic outcomes, including development policies, redistribution, and public finance.
Comparative Politics.Conflict and Peace Studies: Field experiments, observational studies, and survey research on civil wars, ethnic conflict, peacebuilding, and post-conflict governance.
Comparative Politics.Authoritarianism and Democratization: Empirical work on regime transitions, democratization processes, and repression, using cross-national data, experiments, and archival research.

International Relations.Security and Strategy: Quantitative and experimental studies of conflict, deterrence, alliances, and military behavior; includes empirical modeling and historical case analysis.
International Relations.International Politics of Economy: Empirical research on trade, sanctions, and global financial interactions, including field studies, natural experiments, and econometric analysis.
International Relations.Global Governance and Institutions: Data-driven studies on the effectiveness of international organizations, treaties, and global policy interventions.
International Relations.Peacekeeping and Humanitarian Interventi: Observational studies and field experiments evaluating interventions, humanitarian aid, and crisis response effectiveness.

Political Behavior and Public Opinion.Voting and Elections: Survey experiments, field experiments, and large-scale observational studies of voting behavior, turnout, and electoral manipulation.
Political Behavior and Public Opinion.Political Psychology and Attitudes: Lab and survey experiments studying ideology, partisanship, polarization, and cognitive factors in political decision-making.
Political Behavior and Public Opinion.Civic Engagement and Activism: Experimental and observational studies of protests, social movements, online activism, and community participation.
Political Behavior and Public Opinion.Media and Information Effects: Field and lab experiments on political communication, misinformation, social media influence, and framing effects.

Policy and Public Administration.Public Policy Evaluation: Field experiments and quasi-experiments testing the effectiveness of government programs, social policies, and regulatory interventions.
Policy and Public Administration.Bureaucratic and Administrative Processe: Empirical research on bureaucratic efficiency, organizational behavior, and public sector reforms using experimental and observational methods.
Policy and Public Administration.Health, Education, and Social Policy: Experimental and observational studies evaluating the impact of policies on health, education, and welfare outcomes.

Quantitative and Methodological Politica.Experimental Methods: Design and implementation of lab, survey, and field experiments in political science to test causal hypotheses.
Quantitative and Methodological Politica.Survey Research and Cross-National Data: Development and empirical application of survey instruments, cross-national datasets, and measurement techniques.
Quantitative and Methodological Politica.Computational and Network Analysis: Empirical modeling of political networks, social media influence, and agent-based simulations validated with real-world data.

Political Ecology and Environment.Environmental Policy and Climate Politic: Field and survey experiments on environmental regulation, climate policy adoption, and behavioral interventions.
Political Ecology and Environment.Resource Conflict and Management: Empirical studies of political interactions over natural resources, including lab-in-the-field experiments and case studies.
